subject.title: Feature: Per-call cost tracking & auth profile attribution

question: Should OpenClaw make resolved auth-profile attribution part of the canonical completed-model-call accounting contract, and which surfaces may expose it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix affects privacy, billing metadata, transcripts, gateway APIs, diagnostics, plugin contracts, and UI/status behavior, so automation should not choose the exposure boundary.

options.title: Design canonical attribution contract
options.body: Record resolved authProfileId and cost at the normalized completed-call seam, expose only redacted additive readers, and make it the source for status, usage, diagnostics, and plugin views.

options.title: Limit to plugin or diagnostic seam first
options.body: Keep native status and usage unchanged while exposing safe usage metadata through an explicit maintainer-approved plugin observer capability.

options.title: Defer native attribution
options.body: Keep current provider/model summaries and external workarounds until maintainers are ready to design credential-adjacent accounting metadata.

recommendation.title: Design canonical attribution contract
recommendation.body: Record resolved authProfileId and cost at the normalized completed-call seam, expose only redacted additive readers, and make it the source for status, usage, diagnostics, and plugin views.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent history on the usage-cost summaries and has already reviewed this exact issue's missing attribution boundary.
